THE GODS ARE WITH US!.requirements: Mystic archetype, no other talent with the
THE GODS ARE WITH US!.description: Spellcaster keyword You inspire confidence with your fervent calls upon divine favor. You are a spellcaster, as described in more detail in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58. In addition, as a minor action, you can make a Gravitas + Persuasion test with a difficulty of 2. If you pass the test, you and all allies within the same zone each gain +2 Morale resistance until the end of your next turn.

GODS GUIDE YOU.requirements: Mystic archetype, no other talent with the
GODS GUIDE YOU.description: Spellcaster keyword Witnessing the actions of fate and the gods in everything, you can guide the hands of your comrades toward the ordained order. You are a spellcaster, as described in more detail in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58. Additionally, once per round when an ally makes a melee, ranged, or magic attack or performs a Reason + Academia test, you can generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to assist that character as a reaction.

PAIN IS NOTHING.requirements: Mystic archetype, no other talent with the
PAIN IS NOTHING.description: Spellcaster keyword Temporary suffering is nothing in the face of the greater mysteries of the universe. Understanding this allows you to push yourself past the limits of your flesh. You are a spellcaster, as described in more detail in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58. In addition, at the start of any of your turns, you may generate 3 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to remove stress up to your power rating, or to ignore a single injury you've sustained until the end of the current scene.!

AEDIFICATOR.description: You're skilled at the construction of projects both big and small. When you attempt an Engineering-based skill test as part of an extended test that has any resistance, you ignore 1 resistance for each effect you roll.

THE BEST DOCTOR IS ALSO A PHILOSOPHER.description: You've studied the science and philosophies of medicine, including the works of great physicians such as Galen of Pergamon. You are fluent in Greek as an additional language (if you already speak Greek, you may select one additional language to be fluent in). Further, when you make a Medicine-based skill test, you may reduce its difficulty by 1 or 2 at the cost of increasing the skill test's complication range by the same amount.

DEEP EXPERTISE.description: You are an expert in many fields. You gain an additional focus for each skill in which you have 3 or more ranks. After you have taken this talent, each time one of your other skills increases to 3, you immediately gain one additional focus for that skill.

NERO NIHIL VERIUS.description: You have a keen eye that can spot the truth of the matter. Whenever you make a skill test to detect danger or hidden enemies, reduce the test's difficulty by 1.

BACKED BY AUTHORITY.description: You have the backing of a notable regional authority, such as a provincial governor, warlord, or religious figure. You may re-roll 1d20 when you make a Persuasion-based skill test, but you must accept the new result. Additionally, you treat the Restriction rating of all items as 1 lower than normal, to a minimum of 1.

ET TU?.description: You know the best method of attack is with an open hand in front and a dagger clenched behind your back. When you have passed a Persuasion-based skill test to influence or deceive an enemy during a scene, if you make a successful surprise attack against them during the same scene (see Surprise Attack on page 158), you may roll +1 on that attack for every effect rolled; effects rolled on these additional dice do not themselves generate additional .

PLAY THE PART.description: You are so familiar with foreign cultures that you have learned to impersonate the members of a broad range of societies. This includes their styles of dress, their speech, and their other mannerisms. When attempting to make use of a disguise, you may substitute your Academia skill for Stealth.

SOCIAL NETWORK.description: Once you have lived in any place for any length of time, you pick up a variety of hangers-on and informants. In any location where you have had downtime (see Downtime on page 60), you have at least one useful contact on tap (see Connections, Reputation, and Favors on page 53); this contact has a relationship classification of fair. In addition, the first bonus d20 you purchase for any skill test you make during downtime is free (see Spending Momentum on page 23), providing the skill test does not involve combat of any kind.

CUNNING FIGHTER.description: When you fight, you use every dirty trick at your disposal, from throwing sand in your opponent's eyes to kicking them in the mentula. When an enemy attempts a melee attack against you and fails to inflict any stress, they lose their Guard (see Reach and Guard on page 42). If your next attack targeting that enemy is successful, the attack inflicts extra equal to your Athletics skill.

HIDDEN BLADE.description: You fight dirty, slitting opponents' veins open with a discreet but nonetheless deadly blade. When making a melee attack, you may generate between 1 and 3 Threat for the GM's Threat pool. On a successful attack, you can add +1 per Threat generated, or you may add one of the following damage effects to your attack per Threat: Intense, Vicious (see Damage Effects on page 40).

OCULUS AURUM.description: You have an eye for valuables-particularly ones that are not well guarded. As a free action, you may generate 1 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to identify the most valuable object within your zone (see Environments and Zones on page 31). If you do so, you may generate 1 more Threat to know its general value and Restriction rating.

UNREMARKABLE.description: Typically falling beneath scrutiny, you have a natural talent for blending in with crowds, which can be useful for sneaking around a city or camp. When you attempt to blend in, you increase the difficulty of any skill tests to notice you by +1.

EYE FOR WEAKNESS.description: You are able to spot vulnerabilities in your quarry's defenses, natural or otherwise. When you spend Momentum to Obtain Information (ask the GM a question; see Spending Momentum on page 23) to study a creature or enemy, until the end of the scene, your attacks targeting that creature gain the Piercing 1 damage effect or deal +1 if your weapon already has the Piercing effect.

STRIKE FROM HIDING.description: The best attack is one sprung when your prey isn't even aware of you. When you make a successful surprise attack on an enemy (see Surprise Attack on page 158), you may roll +1 on that attack for every effect rolled; effects rolled on these additional dice do not themselves generate additional .

SURVIVALIST.description: You're able to get by in the wilderness using your survival skills to make up for limited resources, and you can operate far afield for extended periods of time. When you make an extended test to forage for food, hunt, build shelter, or gather supplies in the wilderness, you gain the Vicious damage effect on the test.

WOODLAND STRIDE.description: You are proficient in navigating broken and difficult terrain, including dense forest and tangled undergrowth. When you move through difficult or hazardous terrain, you decrease the difficulty of any skill tests you make to move through it by 1, to a minimum of 0. If that difficulty is reduced to 0, you can move through the area as if it weren't difficult or hazardous terrain.

BRUTE.description: Your blows strike deep, opening brutal wounds in your targets. When you perform a melee attack, you can re-roll any number of when determining the stress and damage effects inflicted.

FLASHING STEEL.description: When you perform an Attack major action, you can make a second attack targeting a different character within Reach as a minor action. If you attack a mob of enemies (see the Cohors Cthulhu Gamemaster's Guide, page 189), you instead double the points of stress dealt by your attack.

HOLD FAST.description: You can hold a position against the most brutal of enemy onslaughts, inspiring your allies to do the same. When you or an ally in the same zone is the target of a melee attack, you may generate 1 Threat for the GM's Threat pool. If you do, the attacker adds +1 to the difficulty of their attack.

SHIELD WALL.description: You are trained to fight in formation with your shield-bearing comrades. When you and at least one other ally within Reach are equipped with shields, as a minor action, you can close formation to lock shields with your allies to form a shield wall. Provided they have Guard, each character in the shield wall increases the normal Cover resistance from their shield by +2 while they remain in the shield wall.

ADVISOR.description: You've got a knack for guiding others through problems. When you select this talent, choose a single skill. Whenever you assist an ally and you use that skill, the ally you assist may re-roll a single d20 in their dice pool.

BOLD.description: When you take calculated risks, you tend to succeed more often than seems reasonable. When you select this talent, choose a single skill. When you make a skill test using that skill, and you buy additional d20s by generating Threat for the GM's Threat pool, you may re-roll a single d20 in that dice pool.

PRODIGIALIS FORTUNA.description: The gods who control fate are entertained by you, casting you about on the tides of luck both good and ill. Whenever you spend a Fortune point, you may roll 1 . If you roll an effect , you immediately regain that Fortune point. If you roll a blank, however, you immediately generate 3 Threat for the GM's Threat pool.

SKIN OF YOUR TEETH.description: You have a knack for (just barely) avoiding the worst injuries. Once per scene, you may spend a Fortune point when you are dealt an injury in order to avoid suffering that injury.

CAUTIOUS.description: You're patient and circumspect, acting only when the odds are in your favor. When you select this talent, choose a single skill. When you make a skill test using that skill, and you buy additional d20s by spending Momentum, you may re-roll a single d20 in that dice pool.

APPLIED KNOWLEDGE.description: The knowledge you have accumulated gives you bursts of insight to deal with unexpected challenges. Once per scene, you may use Academia in place of another skill when you make a skill test, and you are counted as having a focus for that test.

COLLABORATION.description: You paid attention to your tutor, were extensively self-taught, or both. You have constantly sought out knowledge beyond the scope of your minimum necessary training. If you pass an Academiabased skill test, you gain +1 bonus Momentum. Bonus Momentum may not be saved.

MAGISTER'S FAVORITE.description: You've coached your allies to capitalize on your expertise, and that effort has paid off. When you select this talent, choose a single skill in which you have 3 or more ranks. Whenever an ally makes a skill test using that skill, and you can communicate with them, you may spend 2 Momentum to allow them to use your ranks in that skill instead of their own, as well as one of your focuses instead of their own (if applicable).

COOL UNDER PRESSURE.description: When the situation gets tough, you take a deep breath and get the job done. When you select this talent, choose a single skill. When you make a skill test using that skill, you may spend a Fortune point to automatically pass that skill test, but you generate no Momentum.

PLATONIST.description: You are skilled at understanding the divide between the utilitarian external world and the internal world of the mind. You gain additional Courage resistance equal to your ranks in Academia. This does not stack with other talents that grant extra Courage resistance.

SAVANT.description: You display an uncommon aptitude. Choose any two skills to which your archetype provided bonus ranks. For each of those skills, you may either increase its ranks by +1 or select a focus for it.

LUDI CHAMPION.description: You have competed, and prevailed, in Rome's annual athletic competition or in its equivalent in another culture. When you make an Athletics-based skill test to run, ride, or swim, ignore the first complication you roll.

MARATHON RUNNER.description: When you are running, you always maintain a reserve of energy to help you cross the finish line. On your turn, you may take the Rush major action even if you have already taken the Movement minor action.

QUALITY CRAFTING.description: The objects, vehicles, and structures you build are a cut above the rest and can withstand much more wear and tear. When you construct an object, its maximum stress increases by +2, and the total number of injuries it can sustain increases by +1. (see Damaging Objects on page 34, for more information on damaging objects.)

THE TOOL FOR THE JOB.description: You're used to putting in hard work and getting the job done. When you make an Engineering-based skill test as part of an extended test, the damage you roll gains the Piercing 1 damage effect.

SCULPTED FROM MARBLE.description: You are a physically remarkable specimen. When you make an Athletics-based skill test to lift, run, throw, or swim, you may re-roll any number of dice on the test.

AGGRESSIVE.description: When you make an attack with a melee weapon, you may reduce the Momentum cost of the first d20 you buy to 0. If you do so, the difficulty of attacks targeting you is reduced by 1 until the start of your next turn. A character with this talent cannot also gain the Defensive talent.

FIELD REPAIR.description: You are adept at repairing items in the field with suboptimal materials. When you make an Insight + Crafting test to repair a damaged item (such as armor or a weapon) in the field, you may generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to reduce the test's difficulty by 1, to a minimum of 1. The repaired item gains the Field Repairs truth.

SCAVENGER.description: You have a knack for finding supplies. By spending half an hour scrounging for useful ingredients and passing an Insight + Crafting test with a difficulty of 1, you can gather enough ingredients to replenish the resources of a crafting tools skill kit.!

DEMOLITIONIST.description: You've got a knack for breaking things. When you make a skill test to attack an object, structure, or stationary vehicle, you may use your Engineering skill instead of Fighting, and you may gain bonus from Reason instead of Brawn or Insight. When you inflict damage on such a target, you may spend 2 Momentum to take any number of rolled up to your ranks in Engineering and replace each with an effect result.

DEFENSIVE.description: You're especially good at avoiding harm. Select melee attacks or ranged attacks. When you are targeted by the selected form of attack, the attack's difficulty increases by +1. This talent may be selected two times, once for each form of attack. A character with this talent cannot also gain the Aggressive talent.

SKIRMISHER.description: One per round when an enemy character misses you with a melee or ranged attack, you may generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool and, as a free action, move to anywhere within Medium range. When you do so, you gain +2 Cover resistance against melee and ranged attacks until the start of your next turn.

STEADY AIM.description: Your attacks with ranged weapons are deadly accurate. When you take the Aim minor action with a ranged weapon, you may re-roll 2d20 on your attack roll that turn, rather than 1d20.

ANATOMIST.description: Your work with injured creatures has given you a working knowledge of how best to injure them. When you attack a human target, or an animal or creature that you have previously dissected, you can land your strikes in vulnerable areas. You can use Medicine instead of Fighting for attacks targeting such creatures and can add the Vicious damage effect to the attacks.

IMPOSING PRESENCE.description: It's always been easy for you to intimidate others. You can use a melee weapon to make a mental attack with a Gravitas + Persuasion skill test. The attack deals mental damage equal to your weapon's + your bonus based on your Will, with your choice of the Piercing 1 or Stun damage effect. You do not need the Fearsome X special rule to make this mental attack.

COMBAT MEDICUS.description: You know the basics of treating wounds in the field. When you use the Stabilize major action, you may re-roll 1d20 from your Coordination + Medicine test. If you pass the test, you may also remove one condition (see Conditions on page 44).

KEEN EYED.description: Your eyesight is as sharp as an eagle's. The increased difficulty of your Perception-based skill tests for zones beyond Close is reduced by 1 (see Distance and Perception on page 31). In addition, when you use a ranged weapon, its normal range and the next higher zone are both considered its effective range. For example, a weapon with an effective range of medium can now be effectively used at both medium and long ranges without an increase in difficulty normally imposed by attacking outside a weapon's effective range.

PREDATOR'S SENSES.description: Your senses are as sharp as those of a wolf on the hunt. While you are conscious, enemies cannot receive the benefits of a surprise attack against you (see Surprise Attack on page 158). Additionally, the gamemaster must spend +1 Threat to have NPCs act first in a combat encounter.

SUSPICIOUS.description: You are suspicious of everything and everyone. You treat every suspicious character (or suspect thicket of brambles) like it might be a threat to your life. Before your turn in the first round of combat, the difficulty of any hostile character's physical or mental attack targeting you increases by +1.

LINGUA ARGENTEA.description: You're blessed with a silver tongue, allowing you to influence people to adopt your views quickly and effectively. When you make a Persuasionbased skill test to sway someone to your way of thinking or haggle over the price of an item, the test's difficulty is reduced by 1.

IRON HIDE.description: You possess great fortitude and can bear horrible injuries without showing it. For the purpose of increasing your complication range, you ignore the first injury you are suffering from. In addition, you are defeated after suffering 4 injuries instead of 3. The GM determines if you are dying or irrational.

MITHRADATIC.description: You are either naturally resistant to toxins or have become inured to them through constant exposure. When you need to make a Resilience-based skill test to avoid the effects of a poison, toxin, or drug, the difficulty is reduced by 1. If this reduces the difficulty to 0, it eliminates the need for a skill test.

SECOND WIND.description: When you take the Catch Breath major action, roll 1 per your ranks in Resilience. For each effect result this generates, you may remove 1 additional point of stress.

FADE AWAY.description: Once per scene as a minor action, you may generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to slip from sight. If you do, you cannot be the target of an attack (other than attacks with the Area damage effect) until the start of your next turn. If you are in heavy cover, you do not need to generate Threat to use this talent.

LOW PROFILE.description: When you gain Cover resistance, the total Cover resistance gained increases by +1.

BESTIARIUS.description: You aren't alone in the wilderness. You have a nonsapient companion creature that serves as a friend and ally in dangerous times. The companion creature has the Companion Creature profile included in this talent entry or one of the profiles in Appendix B: Companion Creatures on page 211. Your companion creature is treated as an allied non-player character under your command. When you forage for supplies, your companion looks after itself. If your companion is ever slain by enemy action or misfortune, you immediately gain a nonrefreshing Fortune point and have a choice between retraining this talent (and getting a new companion) or replacing this talent with a different talent.

COORDINATOR.description: You are proficient in coordinating the actions of a group working in unison. Anytime you participate in a skill test being made with assistance-even if you are not the assisted skill test's leader- the player of each assisting or leading character may choose to re-roll 1d20 but must accept the new result.

INCONSPICUOUS.description: You know how to keep a low profile and avoid suspicion. When your weapons or equipment generate Threat, you reduce the total Threat by 1. Note that if a relic or profane item has a special rule that allows it to generate additional Threat, you cannot reduce the Threat of that object below 1.

UNTRACEABLE.description: You know how to move through the wilderness without leaving a trace of your passage. When you are traveling alone or leading a group, you can increase the difficulty of skill tests to track your movements by half your ranks in Survival, rounding down.

RALLYING CRY.description: With a confident yell, you can stop your comrades from quaking in their caligae (sandal-style hobnailed boots). To use this talent, roll a number of equal to your ranks in Tactics.!Instead of inflicting stress on your stress track, each point of stress generated by the roll lets you or an ally within Close range remove 1 stress. Each roll of lets you remove 2 stress instead of 1. You may apportion the total points of stress removed among yourself and your allies within Close range in any way you choose.

BIZARRE INSIGHT.description: Your mind often shows you glimpses of things you couldn't otherwise know. Once per scene, you may generate 1 Threat for the GM's Threat Pool to Obtain Information (ask the GM a question; see Spending Momentum on page 23) without passing a skill test.

FOREBODING SURVIVAL.description: Every so often, it feels like you narrowly avoid disaster thanks to an unknown guiding hand. How you avoid these fates is unknown, but bad luck seems to befall those around you. Once per session when you are dealt an injury, you may generate 3 Threat for the GM's Threat pool in order to avoid suffering that injury. At the GM's discretion, you may be offered the chance to avoid other misfortune in exchange for generating 3 Threat as well.

MYSTICAL POWER.description: You may select this talent only if you are a spellcaster. You have delved deep into the immortal mysteries of the Mythos and the secrets of time and have returned with a greater aptitude for magical endeavors. You gain an additional personal truth: Glimpsed What Mortals Should Not Know or another truth that reflects the toll this knowledge has taken. When you cast a spell, you may increase your power rating by +2 . If you do so, each of your allies within Close range suffers 1 mental stress for each effect you roll as part of the spell's cost, as they're exposed to the unearthly secrets you have learned.

NUMB TO THE HORRORS.description: For some reason, blood, death, and violence don't affect you mentally. You increase your Courage resistance by +6, but you cannot add any other source of Courage resistance. In addition, you may re-roll 1d20 on any skill test to determine whether you gain a mental scar. However, others find your distant manner off-putting, which increases the complication range of all Persuasion-based skill tests you make by +1.

OCCULT DABBLER.description: You've dabbled with occult forces beyond your comprehension. You are now a spellcaster of the dabbling spellcaster type, as described in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58).

SPECTRAL HUNTER.requirements: Mystic archetype, no other talent with the Spellcaster keyword
SPECTRAL HUNTER.description: You are a spellcaster, as described in more detail in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58. In addition, when you take stress from the cost of a battlefield spell, you can immediately move to anywhere within Medium range. If you already have a talent with the Spellcaster keyword, you may discard it and replace it with this one. A character may have only one talent with the Spellcaster keyword.

HASTY RITUAL.description: Choose one spell that you know. Once per scene, you can cast the chosen spell without first performing the Prepare minor action. When you do so, the spell is cast as a flawed spell (see Flawed Spells on page 61).

INSTINCTIVE MAGIC.description: Once per scene, when you cast a battlefield spell, you may use Resilience (the Fortitude focus applies) instead of any other skill. In addition, the spell's cost is reduced by 2, to a minimum of 1.

JAWS OF THE WOLF.description: When you successfully cast an attack spell, you gain +1 bonus Momentum, which may only be used to add +1 to the damage the spell inflicts on the target.

LUPERCALIA.description: Lupercalia is the great festival for which your college of priests exists. This ceremonial ritual has made you skilled at the working of ritual magic. Whenever you pass one of a ritual's component skill tests, you may ignore up to 2 resistance for every effect rolled.

WOLF HOWL.description: You can invoke the mighty she-wolf of Rome, growling a warning that scratches at the rationality of foes who hear it. You can perform a mental attack targeting a creature you are aware of, and which is aware of you, within Medium range by making a Will + Persuasion or Will + Survival test with a difficulty of 1 (you do not need the Fearsome X special rule to make this mental attack). Passing the test means you inflict power +2 mental damage on your target.

QUIET WISDOM.description: You are a spellcaster, as described in more detail in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58. In addition, you may re-roll 1d20 when you make a Persuasion-based skill test, but you must accept the new result. If you already have a talent with the Spellcaster keyword, you may discard it and replace it with this one. A character may have only one talent with the Spellcaster keyword.

KNOW THE SIGNS.description: You have personally dealt with the effects of the supernatural and recognize the signs of its activity. You are a spellcaster, as described in more detail in Chapter 4: Magic on page 58. In addition, whenever you are in the presence of a person or object that has been affected by supernatural abilities within the last six hours, you may make an Insight + Observation test with a difficulty equal to the number of hours that have passed since the person or object was affected. If you pass the skill test, you recognize the taint of the supernatural. Spending 2 Momentum lets you identify the specific powers used on the person or object. If you already have a talent with the Spellcaster keyword, you may discard it and replace it with this one. A character may have only one talent with the Spellcaster keyword.

DO WE FEAR THIS?.requirements: Force of Presence talent or Protective Superstitions talent
DO WE FEAR THIS?.description: You can easily buoy the spirits of your allies, imbuing them with a sense of purpose that lets them endure great adversity. As a minor action, you may spend 1 Fortune point to grant each of your allies within Close range a bonus to Morale resistance equal to your ranks in Persuasion. This bonus lasts until the end of the scene.

FORCE OF PRESENCE.description: Your bonus damage for attacks that deal mental damage increases by +1.

RUNECASTING.requirements: Quiet Wisdom talent or Know the Signs talent
RUNECASTING.description: You know how to cast the runes to scry for future events. Once every twenty-four hours, you may cast the runes. Make an Insight + Observation test with a difficulty between 1 and 5 (your choice). If you pass the test, roll a number of d20s equal to the test's difficulty and record the result of each die rolled. At any point until the next morning, you may use the following reaction: when you, or any creature you can perceive within line of sight, makes a skill test, you may change one or more of the d20s rolled to match one of your previously recorded results. Each recorded result may be used to change a single d20 only. You do not have to use all the recorded results on a single test.

PROTECTIVE SUPERSTITIONS.description: When you resist a spell (see Resisting Magic on page 66), you gain +1 bonus Momentum per rank in Observation.

FABRICATOR.description: You may re-roll 1d20 when you make a Crafting- or Engineering-based skill test, but you must accept the new result.

DEDICATION.description: Your commitment to a cause is unwavering, and this has carried you through many a tough situation. At the start of a scene, if there is no Momentum in your group's Momentum pool, roll 1d20. If you roll equal to or less than your Will rating, add +1 Momentum to your group's Momentum pool.

IN THE NICK OF TIME.requirements: Intense Study talent, 3+ ranks in Academia or Engineering
IN THE NICK OF TIME.description: Whenever you pass an Academia- or Engineering-based skill test as part of an extended test, you gain the Vicious damage effect on the test.

INCISIVE SCRUTINY.description: You have a knack for finding weak spots in arguments, theories, and machines alike to glean information from them, learning about things by observing how they respond to pressure against vulnerable points. When you pass an Insight- or Reason-based skill test, you gain +1 bonus Momentum, which may be used only for the Obtain Information Momentum option.

INTENSE SCRUTINY.requirements: (Incisive Scrutiny talent or Intense Study talent) and 3+ ranks in Academia or Engineering
INTENSE SCRUTINY.description: When you pass a Reason- or Will-based skill test as part of an extended test, you gain the Piercing 2 damage effect on the test.

INTENSE STUDY.requirements: Dedication talent or Intense Scrutiny talent
INTENSE STUDY.description: You are extremely well-read, possessing vast amounts of knowledge on a wide range of subjects that can provide you with situational expertise in times of need. Twice per game session, before you make a skill test, you may choose a focus you do not possess and gain it for that test. You then retain the focus for the remainder of the session.

PHYSICIAN.description: You may re-roll 1d20 when you make a Medicine-based skill test, but you must accept the new result.

EMERGENCY DOCTOR.description: When you take the Stabilize major action, the difficulty is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

FAST AID.description: When you make a Medicine-based skill test, you may choose to suffer one additional complication in exchange for gaining one automatic success on the test.

FIELD MEDICINE.description: When you make a Medicine-based skill test, you may ignore any increase in difficulty for working without the proper tools or equipment.

FIRST RESPONSE.requirements: Fast Aid talent, 3+ ranks in Medicine
FIRST RESPONSE.description: In combat, you may use the Stabilize major action on characters who are not dying: if you pass a skill test to perform this action, your target does one of the following (your choice): removes stress equal to your ranks in Medicine and removes 1 additional point of stress per Momentum spent; removes a condition; or removes an ongoing damage effect, such as the Persistent damage effect, that is currently afflicting them.

TRIAGE.requirements: Emergency Doctor talent or First Response talent, 3+ ranks in Medicine
TRIAGE.description: You can make a Reason + Medicine test to identify specific injuries or illnesses in a patient, or to determine the severity of a patient's condition. If you do so, you gain +1 bonus Momentum, which you may use only on the Obtain Information Momentum option. In addition, when you pass a Reason + Medicine test to remove a scar, you can remove the scar of one additional patient for each Momentum spent.

SHARP SENSES.description: You may re-roll 1d20 when you make an Observation-based skill test, but you must accept the new result.

DO OR DIE.description: Frumentarii are used to operating independently and know they are likely to be cut off from support much of the time. Such is their determination that they may generate 1 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to gain +2 Morale resistance until the end of the current scene.

INTERROGATION.description: When you pass a skill test to coerce someone to reveal information in a social conflict, you gain +1 bonus Momentum, which you may spend only on the Obtain Information Momentum option.

KNOW THY ENEMY.description: When you make an Insight-based skill test to determine whether someone is lying or hiding the truth, the first d20 you buy does not cost you Momentum.

PERFECT FACADE.description: You have learned to capably impersonate a broad range of people, effectively blending into the background and appearing as though you belong. When you pass a Stealth-based skill test to make or use a disguise, you gain bonus Momentum equal to your ranks in Stealth, to a maximum of +3 bonus Momentum.

THOROUGH SEARCH.description: When you pass a skill test to search an area for evidence, you generate +1 bonus Momentum, which you may use only on the Obtain Information Momentum option. If you assist another character on a skill test to search an area for evidence, and they pass their skill test, then that character receives this talent's +1 bonus Momentum, which is subject to the same restriction.

CHARISMATIC.description: You may re-roll 1d20 when you make a Persuasion-based skill test, but you must accept the new result.

COMMANDING PRESENCE.description: You lead with immense charisma and persuasive skills. When you make a Persuasion- or Tactics-based skill test, the first d20 you buy does not cost you Momentum.

HONESTAS.description: You maintain a careful air of respectability. Whenever you make a skill test to resist being coerced into breaking a promise, betraying your allies, or otherwise acting dishonorably, the difficulty is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

LICTORS.description: You may designate any number of allied characters in your zone up to your rank in Tactics to act as your lictors. For the remainder of the scene, whenever you are targeted by an attack, one of your lictors can choose to be the target instead; the lictor gains Courage resistance against that attack equal to your ranks in Tactics.

RHETORIC.description: When you make a skill test to speak to a crowd, if you buy any bonus d20s, you may re-roll a single d20.

STOIC.description: You subscribe to the philosophy of Stoicism, being indifferent to the vicissitudes of fortune and to pleasure and pain. The difficulty of all skill tests you make to resist coercion, mental intrusion, pain, or other mental attacks is reduced by 2, to a minimum of 0.

HASTY RETREAT.description: When you make a skill test to evade pursuit, if you buy any bonus d20s, you may re-roll a single d20.

INCONSPICUOUS (ROBBER).description: Committing a crime is easy-getting away with it is harder. Through practice, you have learned how to avoid notice and slip away undetected. If any people who aren't your enemies are within Close range of you, you may make an Insight + Stealth test to hide or avoid notice even if you are visible to an enemy. The GM may increase the difficulty of this test if your appearance, clothing, or similar stand out or are likely to draw undue attention.

ALTER EGO.description: You can adopt an alter ego: another "I." Whenever you enter a scene, you may choose an identity or persona to adopt. If you do, you receive a new truth that represents who you appear to be, and you retain this truth until you are discovered or choose to drop your disguise. If you move out of sight of others during a scene, you may take a major action and generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool in order to quick-change into a new disguise.

NIMBLE.description: You're quick on your feet, and few obstacles can impede you. When you make a skill test to move over, around, or through difficult terrain or similar physical obstacles (such as during a pursuit or skirmish), the difficulty is reduced by 2. If this reduces the test's difficulty to 0, you may move over or around that obstacle freely, as if it weren't there.

RANSACK.description: When time is of the essence, you prioritize getting the work done over covering your tracks. When you make an Observation-based skill test to search an area, you may generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to reduce the test's difficulty by 1 and halve the amount of time the search takes.

SCOTOPIA (ROBBER).requirements: Alter Ego talent or Nimble talent
SCOTOPIA (ROBBER).description: Your eyes are accustomed to the dark. You ignore any penalties to skill tests imposed due to poor illumination or low light levels. This talent does not help you in total darkness, however.

SUBTLE STEP.description: You're well versed in methods for avoiding notice, and you reveal little that you do not intend. When you make a Stealth-based skill test to sneak or otherwise pass unseen through an area, the first d20 you buy does not cost you Momentum.

ASSASSIN.requirements: Death Dealer talent or Silent Strike talent
ASSASSIN.description: You are practiced in the art of murder, and taking lives no longer carries emotional weight for you. When you attack with a melee weapon that has the Hidden weapon quality, you may spend 2 Momentum to count the result of each blank rolled in your dice pool as an effect instead of the die's actual roll.

BACKSTABBER.requirements: Guard Break talent or Subtle Step talent
BACKSTABBER.description: When you attack a target that does not have Guard, your weapon's attacks gain the Intense damage effect if they do not already have that effect.

DEATH DEALER.requirements: Guard Break talent or Silent Strike talent
DEATH DEALER.description: You are a proficient killer, relying on trickery and misdirection. When you are armed with any weapon that has the Hidden weapon quality, you may use your Stealth skill instead of your Fighting skill to attack with that weapon, and you may increase that weapon's damage by +1.

GUARD BREAK.requirements: Backstabber talent or Subtle Step talent
GUARD BREAK.description: When you attack an opponent with a Reach greater than yours, treat the opponent's Reach as 1 point lower.

SILENT STRIKE.requirements: Backstabber talent or Death Dealer talent
SILENT STRIKE.description: Each attack you make with a melee weapon that has a Reach of 1 gains the Subtle weapon quality.

TRACKER.description: When you make a skill test to discover or follow tracks, the first d20 you buy does not cost you Momentum.

CONSTANTLY WATCHING.description: When you make a skill test to detect danger or hidden enemies, the difficulty is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

DEAD EYE.description: You know where to sink your shots to do the most damage. When you attack with a ranged weapon, the weapon deals an extra +1 damage.

EXPERT AIM.description: When you take a moment to aim, you rarely miss even the most challenging targets. When you take the Aim minor action, instead of re-rolling 1d20, you may select a single d20 in your dice pool before rolling and count that die as having rolled a 1.

SCOTOPIA (HUNTER).description: Your eyes are accustomed to the dark. You ignore any penalties to skill tests imposed due to poor illumination or low light levels. This talent does not help you in total darkness, however.

SELF-SUFFICIENT.description: You may re-roll 1d20 when you make a Survival-based skill test, but you must accept the new result.

PACK TACTICS.description: When you assist another character during combat and they pass their skill test, the character you assist generates +1 bonus Momentum.

ACROBATIC DODGE.description: You're always moving, and you have a knack for recognizing opportunities to escape an aggressive enemy. When an enemy makes a melee attack against you, you may oppose the attack with Agility + Athletics instead of Agility + Fighting. You may not inflict damage if you win this opposed test, but you may move to any point within Close range; if you spend 1 Momentum after winning this opposed test, you may move to anywhere within Medium range instead.

ASSAIL.description: Velites are known for unleashing a rain of javelins the moment before they charge into combat. When you make a ranged attack with a weapon that has the Thrown Weapons focus, you may spend 2 Momentum to take a second major action that turn.

FORTUNE FAVORS THE BOLD.description: When you fail a skill test and spend Fortune to re-roll dice, before you re-roll, you can choose to increase the difficulty of the test by +1. If you do so and the re-rolled dice let you pass the test, you immediately regain the spent Fortune.

REJUVENATION.description: Used to strings of clashes at the edges of the battlefield, Velites know how to quickly get back into the fray. When you take the Catch Breath major action, the difficulty of the skill test to do so is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0; in addition, each Momentum you spend to remove stress as part of this action removes 2 stress instead of 1.

SWIFT VICTORY.description: There is value in speed, even if there are consequences. When you make an Athletics-based skill test to take a Rush major action or to cross difficult terrain, you may choose to suffer one additional complication in exchange for gaining one automatic success on the test. Further, at the start of any conflict, you may generate 1 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to take the first action, regardless of who would otherwise act first.

HEAD TAKER.description: Choose a single Toughened or Nemesis NPC you can perceive within line of sight. Your melee attacks gain +1 against the chosen NPC. This effect lasts until the chosen NPC is dead, until the end of the scene, or until you suffer stress from an attack the chosen NPC makes. You gain +1 nonrefreshing Fortune point when you defeat the chosen NPC, which you lose at the end of the current scene.

WAR CRY.description: When the chosen NPC from your use of the "Head Taker" talent targets you with a melee attack, you may bellow a war cry as a reaction. Before the GM rolls the dice pool for the chosen NPC's attack, you may choose 1d20 from that dice pool. That die is not rolled, and it instead counts as if it had rolled a 20. Additionally, the complication range of the chosen NPC's attack increases by +1.

HACK AND SLASH.description: When you make a melee attack targeting a creature you have already hit with a melee attack during the current scene, the first d20 you buy does not cost you Momentum.

BRUTAL FIGHTER.description: All weapons you wield gain the Vicious damage effect. If a weapon already has the Vicious damage effect, its damage increases by +2 when you use it.

BLOODY-HANDED.description: When you make a melee attack, you may add the Area damage effect to the attack, striking one extra target (an opponent chosen by the GM) within Close range for each effect rolled. If you do so, you also add 1 Threat to the GM's Threat pool for each effect rolled. The GM may spend Threat from your use of this talent to cause your attack to hit secondary targets you did not wish to strike: each unintended target costs the GM 2 Threat.

ONSLAUGHT.description: After you make a melee attack and your opponent takes stress from that attack, you may move anywhere within Medium range as a free action.

BERSERKER RUSH.description: After you use the Rush major action, you may spend 2 Momentum to make a melee attack at the end of your movement. If your target takes damage from this attack, the attack deals +1 to the target.

LEGIONARY TRAINING.description: You may re-roll 1d20 on any Fighting-based skill test you make with a spear, gladius, or pilum, but you must accept the new result.

LEGIONARY VETERAN.description: You have endured many hardships as a legionary, giving you an iron resolve. Increase your Courage resistance by +2.

PRECISION STRIKES.description: The weapons you wield gain the Piercing 1 damage effect. If a weapon already has the Piercing damage effect, increase Piercing by +1.

STRIKE AS ONE.description: As a minor action before making an attack, you may spend one or more Momentum to give an order to strike to one ally per Momentum spent; the maximum Momentum you may spend here is equal to your Tactics rank. When you then make an attack (as a major action as normal), each ally who received the order may use their Reaction to make a melee attack or ranged attack.

SCUTARIUS.description: As a major action, you may lock shields with an allied character in the same zone. To do so, you and your ally must each have a shield equipped. While your shields are locked together, you gain an additional +X Cover resistance, where X is Shield X weapon quality of your ally's shield; your ally in turn receives an additional bonus to Cover resistance equal to your shield's Shield X quality.

BRACE FOR IMPACT.description: When you are targeted by a melee attack but before the attack's dice pool is rolled, you may brace yourself in formation with an allied character in the same zone. To enter the formation, you and your ally must each have a shield equipped. You and your ally each gain +1 Cover resistance. If you win the melee attack's opposed Agility + Fighting test, you may inflict damage on your opponent and force them to fall back to a point you choose within Close range.

FORMATION TACTICS.description: As a major action, you may enter a formation with an allied character in the same zone. To enter the formation, you and your ally must each have a shield and gladius or similar sword equipped. While you are in this formation, you can regain Guard as a free action even if you have an enemy within Reach. Further, if an enemy makes a successful attack against anyone in this formation, that enemy suffers 2 physical damage.

PURSE STRINGS.description: As a reliable member of the Servant caste, you have been entrusted with your employer's household financial matters, which you can use to your own advantage. Once per adventure, you may purchase an item with a Restriction rating of 3 or lower using your employer's wealth or requisition points instead of your own wealth or your requisition points. You either remove the item from your employer's possession or purchase it on their behalf and "borrow" it for a short time. You must return the item to your employer's control following the current adventure.

ENVY AND ATTENTION.description: You hold considerable status in society, and while that comes with numerous benefits, it can cause challenges and complications to arise as well. Whenever you attempt a skill test to sway opinion or influence others using Gravitas, the cost to buy the first bonus d20 on that skill test is reduced to 0, but the GM begins each adventure with +2 additional Threat in their Threat pool to represent these potential problems. This talent cannot be retrained (see Retraining on page 144) unless your character loses their position as a member of the Noble caste.

ALEA IACTA EST (THE DIE IS CAST).description: Once per scene when an NPC suffers a complication, you can use this talent to increase the GM's Threat cost to cancel the complication to 4 Threat.

ALL ROADS LEAD TO ROME.description: The Roman Empire is vast and includes a wide variety of peoples, with different cultures, languages, and traditions. When you make a skill test to learn about an unfamiliar culture, or to act in an appropriate manner when interacting with members of such a culture, the test's difficulty is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

UNYIELDING.description: You are made of sterner stuff than most. You increase your maximum stress by +3.

WOODWISE.description: When you are in the woodlands of Germania and make a skill test to find food or shelter, to navigate, or to travel in the forest, the difficulty of the test is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

BALANCING THE SCALES.description: The people of Ægyptus have a long history of understanding the balance between one's good and ill deeds, stretching back to stories of Anubis weighing the hearts of the dead in the afterlife. When you make a skill test to haggle for the price of a good or service, you can generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool to reduce the difficulty of the test by 1, to a minimum of 1.

WRIT IN STONE.description: Your homeland is known for its long history, some of which is etched into stone on the faces of ancient walls. When you make an Academia-based skill test to recall a bit of relevant history or lore, you may re-roll each d20 that fails to generate a success.

NIGHT RAIDERS.description: The people of Britannia, particularly those in the northern regions, are skilled at fighting in the dead of night. Your keen night sight allows you to ignore location truths that modify skill tests imposed due to poor illumination or low light levels. This talent does not help you in total darkness, however.

WARRIOR BORN.description: A true child of Andraste, you are fearless and relentless on the attack. You begin the game with +2 Courage resistance.

NOBLE LINE.description: The people of Gaul have a long lineage of respected noble leaders. You may re-roll 1d20 on any test you make to gain support or aid from a non-Roman, but you must accept the new result.

UNDERGOING ALL DANGERS.description: Some claim that the people of Gaul once burned down their former homes before they migrated, in the belief that destroying the hope of return would compel them to face any hardship. You begin the game with +1 Courage resistance.

COSMOPOLITAN.description: Your homeland supports countless visitors and residents with a dazzling variety of customs and tongues. When you speak with someone with whom you do not share a language, you are both nevertheless able to clearly communicate with each other through a combination of pidgin, gestures, and other means, provided the information is not overly complex.

PRACTICED LISTENER.description: Your homeland is rife with the great thinkers of the age, each with their own unique perspective on truth. Hearing their words in the streets of Greece and at the forum have given you keen insight. When you make an Insight-based check to determine the honesty of a speaker, you may re-roll a d20 that fails to generate a success.

DO AS THE ROMANS DO.description: Learning to live among the people of Rome is a useful talent for anyone who resides in proximity. You gain access to any of the culture talents available to Roman citizens. Choose one Roman culture talent.

HIDDEN POTENTIAL.description: Once per scene, you can generate 2 Threat for the GM's Threat pool. If you do, for the remainder of the scene, you can choose one skill in which you do not have ranks and treat it as if you have 2 ranks in the chosen skill, plus one focus appropriate for the chosen skill.

WORLD-WEARY.description: When you make a Will-based skill test, you add one automatic success to the test. After putting up with the headaches of life under Roman rule, you tend to remain unfazed.
